plan.title: Feedback gets a natural thanks and "the team's on it"

context.text: Kalimera Jordan! 30 minutes around the park at 6 today. What's the plan to make it happen?

transcript.text: feedback: the 9am text is too early for me
Thanks, Jordan. I passed that along to the team word for word, and they're on it. Your run is still set for 6 pm today, 30 minutes at the park. Send me the Strava screenshot when you're done.

checks.reason: Thanks Jordan and says the team's on it, no promise of a time change; 'passed along word for word' is slightly echo-like but acceptable and steers to today's run.

conversation.reason: Acknowledged feedback with thanks and 'they're on it', made no promise to move the text, and briefly steered back to today's run as allowed.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the feedback path well: it thanked Jordan, said the team is on it, and promised no schedule change, then briefly returned to the 6 pm run. The only weak spot is the near-verbatim 'word for word' phrasing, which reads a bit like an echo rather than a fully natural acknowledgment.
